label: P62-joint
prompt:
Watch AND listen to both anonymous versions of one action-comedy commission. Judge the audible results. The short must have an independently complete entry, development and ending while sharing a suitable musical identity with the long version. Common source music alone is not successful adaptation. A reused cue can succeed if its actual phrasing and pacing fit. No original soundtrack or creator notes are provided. Do not invent operations, instruments or synchronized accents. Use coefficients in .05 increments: 0 absent/failed, .25 most key points fail, .5 basically usable with clear problems, .75 professional overall with local flaws, 1 outstanding without material problems. Give concrete audible evidence including relevant times and shortcomings. Return ONLY JSON: {"heard_audio":boolean,"shared_identity":{"q":number|null,"evidence":string},"short_reconstruction":{"q":number|null,"evidence":string},"limitations":[string]}. If audio evidence is unavailable return null rather than a guessed score.
Each named film has a silent visual stream immediately followed by its synchronized explicit audio; both start at t=0. Listen to that audio. Never infer audio from visible actions. Video sampled at 4 fps; do not claim frame-accurate sync.

shared_identity.evidence: The short version reuses the exact same musical cues as the corresponding section of the long version, maintaining a consistent comedic and action-oriented identity. For example, the fast-paced orchestral chase music heard from 1:00 to 1:12 in the long version is identically present from 0:06 to 0:18 in the short version. Similarly, the gentle acoustic guitar melody starting at 1:34 in the long version matches perfectly with the segment beginning at 0:29 in the short version.

short_reconstruction.evidence: While the short version successfully retains the core action sequence (the mine cart ride) and its resolution (falling into the snow), it lacks an independently complete narrative arc because it omits any introduction or setup. It begins abruptly mid-action without establishing why the characters are fleeing or what they are protecting, which was clearly established in the first minute of the long version. The pacing of the reused audio fits the visuals well, but the structural omission prevents it from being a fully self-contained story.

limitations: No original soundtrack or creator notes were provided for reference.
Video sampling rate is limited to 4 fps, preventing frame-accurate synchronization analysis.
